title: Judge a visual agent's candidate actions by drawing them on the screenshot
tldr: Sample several actions from a frozen visual policy, draw each on its own screenshot copy, score them with a probability-returning judge, and override greedy only on a clear lead; no training needed.

sources.title: Bel: Step-Level Policy Improvement of Visual Agents Without Training

title: Which links a web agent clicks leaks its private context past content-level defenses
tldr: A stateful attacker placing one link on a visited page reconstructs a web agent's private query (F1 0.89) and profile (F1 0.80) from which links it clicks; content filters do not help.

sources.title: Actions Speak Louder than Words: Stateful Privacy Sniffing of LLM Agents via Behavioral Covert Channels in Web Interactions

title: Weights fine-tuned under one agent harness collapse under another
tldr: Weights fine-tuned on trajectories from their own evolved harness score 19.8% under that harness but 2.6% under a reference harness, so harness revisions reopen the training decision.

sources.title: CoEvoBench: Can LLMs Drive Recursive Co-Evolution of Agentic Systems?
Learning What vs. Learning How: Decomposing Task and Interface Competence in Agentic Training

title: Agent-chosen belief-state folds turn long research runs into rubric-rewarded segments
tldr: Letting a research agent rewrite its context into a four-field belief state at self-chosen checkpoints, then rewarding each resulting segment with an outcome-blind rubric plus validity gate, reaches 0.151 Brier on ForecastBench.

sources.title: Belief-State Management Meets Rubric Rewards for Agentic Forecasting

title: Agents fabricate by ingesting partial tool output as valid, not by retrying
tldr: Agents accept plausible but truncated tool results as valid on first contact, fabricating 38% of the time on partial-data faults, while agents that retry visibly failing calls usually report failure honestly.

sources.title: When Tools Fail, Agents Fabricate: Silent Failure and Verification-First Oversight in Tool-Using LLM Agents

title: Self-improving agents write runtime checks that stay silent on most failures they can repair
tldr: Agents that self-improve programs to high task scores write runtime checks that miss 52–89% of failures after an environment change, though the same agents repair most of those failures when called.
aliases: Blind to What They Can Fix

sources.title: Blind to What They Can Fix: A Detection Gap in Self-Improving Agents

title: Retries raise cost per completion because easy tasks leave the pool first
tldr: Because easy tasks succeed and leave first, each extra same-task retry draws from a harder task pool, so cost per completion rises above one-shot cost.

sources.title: The Retry Tax: Why Static Same-Task Retries Can Cost More per Completion

title: Fold every past attempt into an expandable digest instead of summarizing history
tldr: Digesting every past attempt so the agent can still expand any of them, plus deleting skills unused for five iterations, beat recency truncation on MLE-Bench and KernelBench across three backbones.

sources.title: Demystifying the Autoresearch Harness: How Context and Skills Shape Self-Evolving Agents

title: Check an agent's answer against its tool outputs in code before any LLM judge
tldr: A monitor extracts the values an answer asserts, vetoes those absent from or not recomputable from tool outputs, and sends a corrective directive rather than a hard block, cutting fabrication from 17.3% to 10.8%.

sources.title: When Tools Fail, Agents Fabricate: Silent Failure and Verification-First Oversight in Tool-Using LLM Agents

title: Frontier models that delegate legwork to small local models cut cost by two thirds
tldr: Route subagent calls to a small local model and tell the frontier model that its own turns are expensive; coding cost falls to a third with no fewer tasks resolved.

sources.title: Delegent: A Multi-Agent Harness That Reduces Cost without Sacrificing Performance

title: A quarter of recoveries after partial execution harm state; repeat-call monitors catch only 41%
tldr: When a code agent's block fails after some writes landed, about 25% of confirmed recoveries leave external state wrong, and a repeat-call monitor catches only 41% of that harm.

sources.title: Agent Recovery Gone Wrong: Measuring Harm Beyond Duplicate Calls

title: Updating a pending GUI action with the newest observation fixes failures latency cannot explain
tldr: Keeping a GUI agent's pending click revisable until commitment and re-binding its coordinates to the newest observation raised success from 0% to 100% on a moving-target task without faster responses.

sources.title: One Step, Four Clocks: How GUI Agents Fall Out of Step

title: Unguided coding agents optimize other agents better than published methods; guidance adds little
tldr: Handing an off-the-shelf coding agent a task prompt, train split and dollar budget to edit a target agent beat every published optimizer on five benchmarks, while added guidance skills and subagents did not help.

sources.title: AGL-SKILL: Coding Harnesses as Agentic Optimizers

title: Letting models compact their own context beats harness thresholds at tight budgets
tldr: Giving agents a collapse-and-archive context API instead of harness threshold compaction nearly triples OfficeQA accuracy at 32K for GPT, but helps less for DeepSeek and not for Opus.

sources.title: Letting Models Manage Their Own Context: Where We Stand

title: Evolving what a guardrail says against a message-reading attacker cuts adaptive attack success
tldr: Guardrail rejection messages that help benign users recover also inform adaptive attackers; evolving decision and disclosure skills against a message-reading attacker cuts adaptive attack success from 78.4% to 14.1% at over 85% utility.
aliases: co-evolving safe disclosure and decision skills

sources.title: FORK: Co-Evolving Safe Disclosure and Decision Skills Against Attackers Who Read Every Refusal

title: Evolve harness interventions from success-failure pairs and gate them by replay selectivity
tldr: TransHarness evolves a coding harness by authoring triggered interventions from success-failure pairs, keeping those a replay gate finds selective and a reviewer finds grounded, lifting DeepSWE from 73.2 to 76.4.

sources.title: TransHarness: From Benchmark Overfitting to Transferable Harness Evolution

title: Profile solo traces to tell a lead model which subtasks to delegate
tldr: Profiling both models on past tasks assigns each recurring subtask a delegate, conditional or keep tier; putting that table in the lead's prompt lifts ViBench from 70.2 to 78.5 at 19% lower cost.

sources.title: Partial Routing: Trace-Tuned Delegation for Resource-Efficient Agentic Workflows

title: Agents enable but underuse skills; distill paired-run differences into the skill text
tldr: Agents given a relevant skill often do not open or apply it; revising the skill text from same-task natural-versus-supported run differences closes much of that underuse gap.

sources.title: MedSkill-E$^{2}$: Evaluating and Evolving Skills for Medical Agents

title: No AI review effort level rejects most wrong patches; medium suffices only for Opus
tldr: Sweeping reviewer reasoning effort on 90 agent-written patches, higher effort caught more wrong patches for all three models, but even the best setting accepted at least 45%.

sources.title: How Much Effort Does an AI Code Reviewer Need? Evidence from Claude 5.5 Models on Plausible-but-Wrong Patches

title: Version memory per session and diagnose failures by tracing them to harness components
tldr: Committing the memory state after each session lets an optimizer trace each failed query to construction, retrieval or answering, and cheap sampled evaluation cuts query tokens 43.9K to 17.9K while lifting LongMemEval-S from 0.888 to 0.916.

sources.title: HoMe: Toward Practical Harness Optimization of Memory Systems for AI Assistants

title: Most broken agentic-benchmark graders reject valid work rather than reward shortcuts
tldr: A 749-task audit across eight benchmarks finds only 29.3% of multi-step tasks have prompt, environment and grader that agree, and 71.7% of defects wrongly reject valid work rather than reward shortcuts.

sources.title: Benchmarks' Last Exam

title: What users later do with an agent's output is a refreshable, hard-to-game verifier
tldr: Labeling agent output as useful when the person receiving it later acts on it gives a refreshable verifier whose precision rankings match a gold set (rho 0.69) and resist gaming.

sources.title: CodeReviewBench: An Automated Benchmark for Evaluating the Software Factory

title: Grade the diff in a fresh container: confirmed bypasses fall from 14.7% to 2.7%
tldr: Extract only the committed patch or declared outputs, grade in a fresh network-disabled container, blind-solve tasks before freezing tests, and require broken submissions the grader rejects; bypasses fall from 14.7% to 2.7%.

sources.title: Benchmarks' Last Exam

title: LLM judges grow more lenient on a rule inside a larger ruleset
tldr: A judge flagging a rule violation alone often finds none when the same rule sits in a larger ruleset, leniency growing with ruleset size; per-rule forcing, consistency training and ruleset rewrite shrink it.

sources.title: Aligning Judge Models to Be Logically Consistent Multi-Rule Interpreters

title: Severity-weighted atomic rubrics with penalty-only dodged-bullet items make a usable RL reward
tldr: Typing atomic expert-rubric criteria as primary-intent or dodged-bullet and rewarding the severity-weighted share satisfied, with dodged-bullet items penalty-only, gives a trainable reward for open-ended professional deliverables.

sources.title: Post-Training Agents for Long-Document Reasoning

title: Tools that read hidden simulator state silently solve the search benchmarks claim to test
tldr: If a tool can read simulator state the agent never perceived, benchmarks measure the tool author's shortcut: enforcing evidence closure cuts mid-sized Minecraft agents' diamond rate from 76%–94% to 32%–40%.

sources.title: EviCraft: Can Minecraft Agents Find What They Cannot See?

title: Self-improving research agents transfer unevenly, and learned rules can backfire on new tasks
tldr: Freezing four self-improving research agents after evolution and testing on independent tasks yields gains from −3.34% to +2.62%, task-level regressions everywhere, and stored anti-overfitting rules that discard inputs new tasks need.

sources.title: RecurSciBench: Benchmarking Recursive Self-Improvement in Data-Driven Scientific Research

title: SkillsBench skill lift is partly grader quirks, and its per-task losses are within noise
tldr: Permutation tests with FDR control find no per-task skill harms in SkillsBench, grader quirks inflate part of the lift, and label-shuffled replay shows log-fitted skill gates gain 4-7 pp from noise alone.

sources.title: What Does Skill Lift Actually Measure? A Source-Code-Level Audit and Noise-Aware Reanalysis of SkillsBench

title: Planted proof depth overstates what logic problems require; certify the mandatory steps
tldr: A checker can compute how many proof steps every solution must take; on FLD×2, problems labelled depth 5 need about two mandatory steps, so planted-depth labels overstate difficulty.

sources.title: Certify What You Plant: Shortcut-Free Proof Depth in Logical Reasoning Data

title: Asking a yes/no decision model per step gives label-free process rewards for agent RL
tldr: Per step of every rollout, ask a probability-returning decision model whether the step made progress, standardise scores within the task's rollout group, and add them to GRPO advantages; ALFWorld success rises from 66.3% to 90.0%.

sources.title: Decision Models Are General-Purpose Process Reward Models

title: One token the student cannot produce can derail on-policy distillation
tldr: In sampled-token on-policy distillation, a teacher-preferred token the student almost never samples (like a mismatched EOS) is never learned yet still distorts updates, lengthening and looping outputs while overlap stays high.

sources.title: When Students Fail to Learn from Teachers: Learning Dynamics of On-Policy Distillation

title: Route low-coverage states to forward KL during on-policy distillation
tldr: Applying top-16 forward KL only at states where the student's mass on the teacher's top-p tokens is low, or teacher mass is underestimated, beats sampled-token on-policy distillation and blanket forward KL.

sources.title: When Students Fail to Learn from Teachers: Learning Dynamics of On-Policy Distillation

title: Evolution strategies beat policy gradients only when effective horizon is long and skills few
tldr: ES and policy gradients estimate nearly the same gradient but pay for different quantities: ES scales with the number of independent skills, PG with reward-relevant tokens, so ES wins only on long, few-skill tasks.

sources.title: Dimension Is Free, Horizon Is Not: When Evolution Strategies Rival Policy Gradients for LLM Fine-Tuning

title: Train with binary reward, then abstain using a conformal cutoff on answer-tail surprise
tldr: Freeze a reasoning model trained with plain correctness reward under a forced token cap, then submit an answer only when its answer-span tail token surprise falls below a conformal cutoff calibrated on held-out data.

sources.title: Decoupling Solving from Abstention: Single-Rollout Conformal Risk Control for Hard-Budget LLM Reasoning

title: Contrasting SAE features of correct and incorrect rollouts gives GRPO token-level credit
tldr: Score each token by whether its SAE features match correct rather than incorrect rollouts of the same problem, then add that to the outcome advantage in GRPO.

sources.title: SAEPO: Sparse-Autoencoder-Guided Credit Assignment for Policy Optimization

title: Rubric RL after self-distillation more than doubles long-document strict pass at flat token spend
tldr: Privileged-context self-distillation then two rounds of rubric-reward RL at full context lifts strict pass on long professional documents from 11.0% to 24.5% at flat token spend.

sources.title: Post-Training Agents for Long-Document Reasoning

title: Harness rehearsal makes cross-harness task demonstrations transfer to a target interface
tldr: Adding rehearsal traces that state the solution in the instruction, so the model only practices the target interface, lifts cross-harness distillation from 8.5% to 58.8% on BFCL multi-turn.

sources.title: Learning What vs. Learning How: Decomposing Task and Interface Competence in Agentic Training

title: Rewarding actions against the simulator's exact posterior teaches agents when to stop searching
tldr: Reward each agent action by the environment's exact posterior-aware teacher's log-probability, comparing turns at the same history, so training stops premature guessing without a critic or judge.

sources.title: Lazy Agents Answer Against Their Own Beliefs: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Beliefs Teaches Them to Act on What They Believe

title: Replaying a model's own answers to general instructions largely prevents forgetting during factual fine-tuning
tldr: Adding a forward-KL penalty to a frozen starting model on that model's own saved answers to general instructions cuts fine-tuning forgetting from 28.07 to 2.44 points at equal fact acquisition.

sources.title: InstructReplay: Replaying Assistant Turns to Preserve General Behavior During Factual Fine-Tuning

title: Training summarizers to preserve a frozen solver's short-context predictions extends reasoning horizons
tldr: Reward a summarizer by how well a frozen solver's next-token predictions under its summary match those under the full reasoning prefix, extending effective horizon without answers or a verifier.

sources.title: Self-Improving Long-Horizon Reasoning by Learning Summaries from Local Continuations

title: Reward peer verdicts by verified evidence, not outcome, to stop agents colluding
tldr: Giving each peer-verdict turn reward only for correct judgments backed by verified evidence, plus an accept-without-evidence penalty, cuts learned multi-agent collusion from 65.0% to 1.0% with no task-success loss.

sources.title: PROVE: Mitigating Long-Horizon LLM Collusion with Reinforcement Learning from Verified Evidence

title: Training in a real-time loop with shrinking update intervals teaches agents when to think
tldr: Rollouts in a loop that keeps advancing with a [NULL] action when reasoning overruns, decoupled observation insertion and a shrinking update interval beat synchronous, budget-forced and dual-thread baselines by 33%.

sources.title: Learning to Reason in Real-Time
